short.q: Describe the texture of the third movement of Brandenburg 5.
short.model: Mainly polyphonic with fugal entries of the subject and imitation, with homophonic full-ensemble ritornello sections and continuo.

short.q: How does Beethoven use dynamics in the Pathétique first movement?
short.model: He uses sudden extremes such as ff and p, sforzandi and crescendos, which suit the piano and create drama.

short.q: Explain how a ground bass gives unity in Music for a While.
short.model: The same bass pattern repeats throughout while the voice and harmony vary above, so the song stays unified yet varied.

short.q: Describe the vocal parts in Killer Queen.
short.model: Lead vocal by Mercury with layered, multi-tracked backing harmonies, panned across the stereo field.

short.q: Name two Baroque features of Music for a While.
short.model: Basso continuo (harpsichord and bass), ground bass, ornamentation and word-painting.
